description: An amendment to H.R. 4389, fiscal 1980 appropriations for the Department of Labor and HEW, that would replace the bill's abortion language with the language restricting abortion in current law.

An amendment to H.R. 2444, a bill to establish a Department of Education. It would bar any institution of higher education that uses mandatory student fees to pay for abortions from using facilities controlled by the Department, except for abortions where the mother's life would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.
A substitute for an amendment to H.R. 4580, the District of Columbia appropriations bill. The substitute would prohibit using funds provided by the federal payment in the bill to perform abortions.

An amendment to H.J.Res. 413, continuing appropriations for Labor and HEW, that would prohibit use of federal funds for abortions except where the mother's life is endangered or in cases of rape or incest.

A motion to concur in Senate amendment no. 137 to H.R. 4389, fiscal 1980 Labor and HEW appropriations, with a House amendment. The Senate amendment permits federal funding of abortion where "medically necessary"; the House amendment would instead prohibit it except where the woman's life would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term, or for victims of reported rape or incest.
Substitute amendments to committee amendments to H.R. 4962, a child health assurance bill, would prohibit funding for medical assistance for abortions except when the woman's life is endangered.

An amendment to H.R. 4962, a child health assurance bill, that would prohibit use of funds to perform abortions except where the life of the mother would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.
An amendment to H.R. 8061, the appropriations bill for the government of the District of Columbia, would prohibit use of any of the bill's funds to pay for abortions.

An amendment to H.R. 3512, a supplemental appropriations bill for fiscal year 1981, that would prohibit the use of funds to pay for an abortion or for administrative expenses of any federal employee health plan that covers abortions after current contracts end.
An amendment to H.R. 3480, the bill reauthorizing the Legal Services Corporation Act, that would prohibit giving legal advice about a client's rights and responsibilities regarding abortion.

An amendment to H.R. 4121, the Treasury and Postal Service appropriations bill, would prohibit use of funds, except where the woman's life is endangered, to pay for an abortion or for administrative expenses of any Federal Employees Health Benefits Program plan that covers abortion.

H.R. 6457 revises and extends National Institutes of Health authorities. A pending substitute would raise biomedical research funds 7 percent and extend expiring NIH authorities, among other changes. This amendment to the substitute would restrict NIH research on fetuses and infants before or after an induced abortion.
An amendment to H.R. 3191 that would prohibit using health benefit funds to pay for abortions unless the woman's life is endangered.

An amendment to H.R. 3913, a bill appropriating $96.16 billion for the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and related agencies for fiscal 1984. The amendment would prohibit use of funds to perform abortions.

An amendment to H.R. 5490, a bill clarifying the application of Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, the Age Discrimination Act and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act. The amendment would define the term "person" to include a fetus from the moment of conception.

An amendment to H.R. 5798, appropriations for the Treasury Department, the Postal Service, the Executive Office of the President and certain independent agencies for fiscal year 1985. The amendment strikes language prohibiting the use of federal health plan benefits to pay for abortions.

A perfecting amendment to a substitute amendment on population planning in H.R. 1555, a foreign assistance bill. It would require nongovernmental foreign-based organizations receiving U.S. funds not to perform or actively promote abortion. The substitute being amended says population planning funds may not be used to pay for abortions as a method of family planning.
An amendment that eliminates the use of federal or local funds for abortions in the District of Columbia except in cases of rape, incest, or danger to the woman's life.
Final passage of H.R. 2713, District of Columbia appropriations for fiscal 1988, which includes a prohibition on using the appropriated funds to pay for any abortions.
An amendment to H.R. 4776, fiscal 1989 District of Columbia appropriations, that would bar the use of funds to perform abortions under any circumstances.

A conference motion on H.R. 4783, the Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations bill, that the House continue to disagree with a Senate amendment permitting Medicaid funds to be used for abortions when pregnancy results from rape or incest.

An amendment to H.R. 2100, the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal years 1992 and 1993, that extends access to abortion and other reproductive health services to service members stationed overseas.

En bloc amendments to H.R. 2039, the Legal Services Reauthorization Act. They would prohibit recipient agencies from using any federal, public, private, or IOLTA funds for litigation or proceedings about abortion, or for lobbying to pass or defeat legislation or regulations about abortion.

An amendment to H.R. 5006, the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal 1993. It would reinstate a Defense Department policy, in effect from 1982 to 1988, allowing overseas military medical facilities to offer abortion services to service personnel and dependents stationed abroad who pay all costs themselves, including indirect costs.

A substitute for a pending amendment to H.R. 4, the National Institutes of Health Revitalization Act of 1993. The substitute restores the fetal tissue research certification requirements and adds a requirement that attending physicians certify that abortions from which fetal tissue is donated for transplant research were performed in accordance with state law.

An amendment to H.R. 4, the National Institutes of Health Revitalization Act, as changed by a substitute. It restores fetal tissue research certification requirements and adds a requirement that attending physicians certify that abortions from which fetal tissue is donated for transplant research were performed under applicable state law.

An amendment, as amended, to H.R. 4, the National Institutes of Health Revitalization Act of 1993. It restores the certification requirements for fetal tissue research and adds a requirement that attending physicians certify that abortions in which fetal tissue is donated for transplant research were performed in accordance with applicable state law.

An amendment to H.R. 2518, the Labor, HHS and Education appropriations bill for fiscal 1994, would provide that none of the funds be spent for any abortion except when the abortion is necessary to save the life of the woman or the pregnancy results from rape or incest.

A separate vote on an amendment to H.R. 2518, Labor, HHS and Education appropriations for fiscal 1994. It provides that none of the funds may be spent for any abortion except when the abortion is necessary to save the life of the mother, or the pregnancy results from rape or incest.

A committee amendment to H.R. 2020, Treasury, Postal Service and general government appropriations for fiscal 1996, that would strike language prohibiting coverage of abortion under federal employees' health insurance policies.

An amendment to H.R. 2020, offered to a committee amendment, that would restrict coverage of abortion under federal employees' health insurance policies except where the woman's life would be endangered or the pregnancy is the result of rape or incest.
An amendment to a committee amendment to H.R. 2020 that would allow coverage of abortion under federal employees' health insurance policies when it is medically necessary.
An amendment to H.R. 1833, a bill to ban "partial-birth abortions", that would clarify how certain provisions apply to abortions necessary to preserve the life or health of the woman.
Final passage of H.R. 1833, a bill to amend title 18 of the United States Code to ban "partial-birth abortions."

An amendment to H.R. 3019 would amend the Public Health Service Act to prohibit governments from discriminating in the training and licensing of health professionals because they refuse to undergo or provide training in performing induced abortions.
A vote to override the President's veto of H.R. 1833, the "Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act of 1995", which amends title 18 of the United States Code to ban "partial-birth abortions".

H.R. 1122 is a bill to amend title 18 of the United States Code to ban "partial-birth abortions". An amendment in the nature of a substitute would replace it with language to prohibit certain abortions.

A substitute amendment to H.R. 1122, a bill to ban "partial-birth abortions". The substitute would instead amend title 18 of the U.S. Code to prohibit performing an abortion once the fetus is determined to be viable.
Final passage of H.R. 1122, a bill to amend title 18, United States Code, to ban "partial-birth abortions."
An amendment to S. 947 would strike the bill's limitation on coverage of abortions.
An amendment to S. 936 that would repeal the restriction on using Department of Defense facilities for abortions.
An amendment to S. 1023 that would prohibit the use of funds to pay for an abortion or for administrative expenses of certain health plans that cover abortions.

An amendment to S. 1061 that would prohibit the use of funds for research using human fetal tissue, cells, or organs obtained from a living or dead embryo or fetus during or after an induced abortion.
An amendment to S. 2057 that would repeal the restriction on the use of Department of Defense facilities for abortions.
A vote to override the President's veto of H.R. 1122, a bill to amend title 18 of the United States Code to ban "partial-birth abortions".
Final passage of S. 1692, a bill to amend title 18 of the United States Code to ban "partial birth abortions."

An amendment to H.R. 4444 requiring the Congressional-Executive Commission on the People's Republic of China to monitor China's cooperation on POW/MIA issues and improvement on forced abortions, slave labor and organ harvesting.
An amendment to H.R. 4444 to express the sense of Congress regarding forced abortions in the People's Republic of China.

An amendment to H.R. 4444 that would require the Congressional-Executive Commission on the People's Republic of China to monitor China's cooperation on POW/MIA issues and improvement in the areas of forced abortions, slave labor, and organ harvesting.

An amendment to H.R. 4444 would require the Congressional-Executive Commission to monitor the People's Republic of China's cooperation on POW/MIA issues and improvement in the areas of forced abortions, slave labor and organ harvesting.
Final passage of S. 3, a bill to prohibit the procedure commonly known as "partial-birth abortion."
The conference report on S. 3, a bill to prohibit the procedure commonly known as partial-birth abortion.
Final passage of H.R. 1997, a bill to amend title 18 of the U.S. Code and the Uniform Code of Military Justice to protect a fetus from assault and murder.

An amendment to S.Con.Res. 18 would expand access to preventive health care services that reduce unintended pregnancy, including teen pregnancy, reduce the number of abortions, and improve access to women's health care.
Final passage of S. 403, a bill to amend title 18 of the U.S. Code to prohibit taking minors across state lines to get around laws requiring parental involvement in abortion decisions.
An amendment to H.R. 976 that would codify what the source calls the "unborn child rule."
An amendment to H.R. 2764 that would prohibit funding of organizations that support coercive abortion.
An amendment to H.R. 2764 would prevent contributions to organizations that perform or promote abortion as a method of family planning.
An amendment to H.R. 3043, an appropriations bill, that would prohibit providing funds to grantees who perform abortions.

An amendment to S.Con.Res. 70 that would increase Department of Justice funding, with an offset, to enforce a prohibition on taking minors across state lines to get around laws requiring parental involvement in abortion decisions, consistent with the Child Custody Protection Act.
An amendment to S.Con.Res. 70 would require that legislation reauthorizing SCHIP include provisions codifying the "unborn child regulation".

An amendment to H.R. 2, a child health assistance bill, that would restore the prohibition on funding nongovernmental organizations that promote abortion as a method of birth control, known as the "Mexico City Policy".
An amendment to H.R. 2 that would codify regulations specifying that an "unborn child" is eligible for child health assistance.
An amendment to H.R. 1105 would require that amounts appropriated for the United Nations Population Fund not be used by organizations that support coercive abortion or involuntary sterilization.

H.R. 7724 provides for a biomedical and behavioral research training program and protections for human subjects. A pending amendment bars research under the bill on a living human fetus or infant delivered by an induced abortion. This second-degree amendment would instead bar federal funds for research and experimentation in the field of abortion until institutional review board certification is established and a national commission develops policies for such research.
An amendment to H.R. 14232 that would delete a section barring the use of funds to pay for abortions or to promote or encourage abortions.

A conference motion on H.R. 14232 that the Senate recede from its amendment and concur in House amendment #68. The Senate amendment would strike a House provision barring the use of funds to pay for abortions or to promote or encourage abortions; receding keeps that House provision in the bill.
A motion that the Senate insist on its amendment to H.R. 14232 deleting a House amendment. The House amendment bans the use of funds to pay for abortions or to promote or encourage abortions.
A vote on the second conference report on H.R. 14232. The conference report contains an amendment that prohibits the use of federal funds to pay for or encourage abortions.
An amendment to H.R. 7555, an appropriations bill, would prohibit the use of funds for abortions except where the woman's life would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.
An amendment to H.R. 7555, an appropriations bill, that would delete the section of the bill restricting the use of federal funds for abortions.

An amendment to H.R. 7555, an appropriations bill, that would allow the use of funds for abortions where the woman's life is endangered, "where medically necessary," or where necessary as treatment for rape or incest.

A motion that the Senate concur in the House amendment to Senate amendment no. 82 to H.R. 7555, the appropriations bill for the Departments of Labor and of Health, Education, and Welfare. Senate amendment no. 82 allows federal funds for abortions when "medically necessary," when the woman's life is endangered, or in cases of rape or incest. The source does not say what the House amendment changes.

A vote on S. Res. 307, instructing the Senate conferees on H.R. 7555, the fiscal 1978 Labor and HEW appropriations bill, to recede from the Senate's amendment on abortion funding. The resolution proposes that the Senate concur in the House amendment authorizing HEW funds for certain "medical procedures" to treat rape or incest victims and for abortions when the mother's life is endangered.

A motion that the Senate concur in an amendment to the House amendment to Senate amendment #82 to H.R. 7555, the Labor and Health, Education and Welfare appropriations bill for fiscal year 1978. As modified, the bill allows funds for medical procedures to treat rape and incest victims, and for abortions where the woman's life would be endangered by the pregnancy or where long-lasting physical health damage to the woman would result if the pregnancy were carried to term.

An amendment to the modified House amendment to Senate amendment no. 82 to H.R. 7555, fiscal 1978 appropriations for the Departments of Labor and of Health, Education, and Welfare. It would authorize use of HEW funds for abortions only if the woman's life would be endangered by the pregnancy "and" if severe and long-lasting physical damage to her would result if the pregnancy were carried to term.
A committee amendment to H.R. 12931, the foreign aid appropriations bill for fiscal year 1979, that strikes language prohibiting the use of Peace Corps funds for abortion.
An amendment to H.R. 12929, an appropriations bill, that would prohibit the use of these funds for abortions except where the life of the mother would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.

An amendment to H.R. 12929 that would prohibit the use of its funds for abortions, except where the woman's life would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term, or where the woman is a victim of rape or incest reported to law enforcement within 48 hours.

An amendment to H.R. 4389 providing federal funding of abortions when the woman's life is endangered, when she is a victim of rape or incest, or when two physicians determine that severe physical health damage would result if the pregnancy were carried to term.
An amendment to H.R. 4580, the fiscal 1980 District of Columbia appropriations bill, would make funding of abortions in the District conform to the abortions funded under the Medicaid program.

A motion that the Senate recede from its amendment No. 137 to H.R. 4389 and accept the House language on Medicaid funding of abortions, which prohibits the use of funds except where the woman's life would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.

A motion that the Senate insist on its amendment no. 137 to H.R. 4389, which restricts Medicaid funding of abortions to cases where the woman's life is endangered or the abortion is medically necessary, or cases of rape or incest.
An amendment to a pending amendment to H.J.Res. 440, a continuing appropriations resolution, would prohibit federal funding of abortions except where the woman's life is threatened.

An amendment to H.J.Res. 610, making appropriations through December 15, 1980. It provides that states remain free not to fund abortions to the extent they deem appropriate, and addresses payments for drugs or devices to prevent implantation of the fertilized ovum and for procedures to end an ectopic pregnancy.
A motion to table the Appropriations Committee amendment to H.R. 3512, a fiscal 1981 supplemental appropriations bill. The committee amendment would use federal funds to pay for abortions.

Passage of S.J.Res. 3, a proposed constitutional amendment establishing legislative authority in Congress and the states with respect to abortion, thereby overturning the Supreme Court's decision in Roe v. Wade.

An amendment to H.J.Res. 413 that would strike funding language taken from H.R. 4139, the Treasury, Postal Service and General Government Appropriations Act, 1984, in its House version. That language related to using federal insurance to pay for abortions.

An Appropriations Committee amendment to H.R. 5175, the District of Columbia appropriations bill. It would replace language barring federal or District funds for abortions except to save the mother's life with language barring only federal funds for abortions, except when the mother's life is endangered or in cases of rape and incest.
An amendment to S. 557, the Civil Rights Restoration Act, to clarify that no part of the legislation requires any individual, program or institution to pay for or perform an abortion.
An amendment to S. 557, the Civil Rights Restoration Act, providing that the act does not require any federally funded individual, program, or institution to perform or pay for an abortion.
An amendment to H.R. 4783, the fiscal 1989 Labor-Health and Human Services-Education appropriations bill, would permit Medicaid-funded abortions for victims of promptly reported rape or incest.

A vote on whether an amendment to H.R. 4404, fiscal 1990 supplemental appropriations, is germane to the bill. The amendment would restrict use of federal funds to perform abortions in the District of Columbia except under certain circumstances.

An amendment to S. 323, the Family Planning Amendments Act of 1992, would provide for referring pregnant individuals for prenatal medical care, including to prenatal care providers who perform abortions, but would prohibit referrals to providers whose principal business is providing abortions.

An amendment to an amendment to S. 323 that would require entities receiving grants under Title X of the Public Health Service Act to provide parental notice or consent when minor patients request an abortion.

An amendment to S. 323, offered to another pending amendment, that would require entities receiving grants under Title X of the Public Health Service Act to provide for parental notification when minor patients request an abortion.
An amendment to a committee amendment to H.R. 2707 that would restrict the use of funds to perform an abortion on a minor under the age of 18.

An amendment to S. 3114, the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal year 1993, would strike provisions allowing military personnel stationed abroad to obtain pre-paid reproductive services, including abortions, in U.S. military hospitals overseas.

A vote on whether an amendment to H.R. 2403, the Treasury, Postal Service, and General Government appropriations bill for 1994, is germane. The amendment would allow employees in the Federal Employees Health Benefits program to buy special riders that cover abortions.
An amendment to H.R. 4426 would prohibit the U.S. government from intervening with respect to abortion laws or policies in foreign countries.

A committee amendment to H.R. 2020, Treasury, Postal Service and general government appropriations for fiscal 1996, that would strike language prohibiting coverage of abortion under federal employees' health insurance policies.

An amendment to H.R. 2020, offered to a committee amendment, that would restrict coverage of abortion under federal employees' health insurance policies except where the woman's life would be endangered or the pregnancy is the result of rape or incest.
An amendment to a committee amendment to H.R. 2020 that would allow coverage of abortion under federal employees' health insurance policies when it is medically necessary.

A conference-stage substitute on abortion funding in H.R. 7555, the fiscal 1978 Labor and Health, Education and Welfare appropriations bill. It would replace a pending amendment with language prohibiting federal funds for abortions unless the woman's life would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.

A perfecting amendment to an amendment on abortion funding in H.R. 7555 that would insert the word "promptly". Its effect is to allow federal funds for abortions if the mother's life would be endangered by the pregnancy, or if she is a victim of rape or incest who has "promptly" reported the incident to a law enforcement or health service agency.

An amendment modifying the House amendment to Senate amendment #82 to H.R. 7555. It authorizes federal funds for abortions if the woman's life would be endangered by the pregnancy, if severe and long-lasting physical health damage to the woman would result, or if the woman is a victim of rape or incest and has reported the incident to the proper authorities.

An amendment to H.R. 12929, an appropriations bill, that would prohibit the use of these funds for abortions except where the life of the mother would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term.
